verdicts.factCheck: On https://forno.celo.org at block 83,494,801 on 2026-11-23: G$.isBlocked(PoolManager) returns 1 and isBlocked of an unrelated address returns 0. paused() returns 0. balanceOf(PoolManager) is 550,022,104,456,118,939,767,246,081, the same value the finding read 4,751 blocks earlier, so no stream runs into or out of the address. eth_call with from set to the PoolManager: transfer to a plain recipient reverts with 0xe7d0c09e for amounts 0, 10^18, one thousandth of the balance and the full balance. transfer(PoolManager, 0) from an unrelated address reverts with the same data, and transfer of 0 between two unrelated addresses returns true. I computed keccak256 of SUPER_GOODDOLLAR_BLOCKED() locally and its first four bytes are e7d0c09e. Both getFees forms return a zero fee. The EIP-1967 implementation slot of the token holds 0xb4419a3df33b9aa6fbe452df8816389e599c29ef, and Sourcify reports a full match for that address under the name SuperGoodDollar (solc 0.8.19). In that source isBlocked is a public mapping (line 48), _processFees calls _onlyNotBlocked for the sender and the recipient before anything else (lines 434 to 440), _onlyNotBlocked reverts with SUPER_GOODDOLLAR_BLOCKED (lines 468 to 470), setBlocked and adminBurn start with _onlyOwner, which requires DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE (lines 365 to 391 and 456 to 458), and adminBurn skips the pause and block checks. The Blockscout log query returns one BlockedUpdated(PoolManager, true) event in block 77,233,730, timestamp 1789134488, which is 2026-09-11 13:48:08 UTC, transaction 0x22cd34a5f179dfa342fd3659d029e4d40469ca8fa02abd032145f162b0b8dd4d. The full list of 52 BlockedUpdated events shows the release transaction of 2026-09-28 in block 78,688,154 and the PoolManager address is absent from it. The GoodLabs post of 2026-10-20 says all liquidity pools were unblocked on 28 September except the Celo Uniswap V4 pool, which holds 550M G$ and remains blocked, and it asks the holder of the position to make contact. The explorer values the balance at about 63,000 USD, third among the ERC-20 balances of the address.
verdicts.codeCheck: take is guarded by onlyWhenUnlocked only. It books the debit and then calls currency.transfer (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). For an ERC-20 the library makes one CALL with selector a9059cbb, and success needs a call that did not revert and returned nothing or a 32 byte 1 (src/types/Currency.sol:60-74). A reverting token makes the take revert with the wrapped ERC20TransferFailed error (src/types/Currency.sol:82-86), which also undoes the debit. No other function sends an ERC-20 out except collectProtocolFees, which uses the same library call (src/ProtocolFees.sol:56). A positive G$ delta can be turned into an ERC-6909 claim by mint or dropped by clear without any token call (src/PoolManager.sol:310-329), and modifyLiquidity makes no token call (src/PoolManager.sol:145-184), so a provider can remove a position and take the other currency. A payment in G$ needs a transfer to the PoolManager between sync and settle (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364), and that transfer reverts while the address is blocked. I found no guard the finding missed.
verdicts.corrections: Step 4 says a sync and settle window can never show an increase. That is too strong. The comment above setBlocked in the verified source (lines 371 to 377) says a blocked account can still be credited by agreements. I did not simulate a Superfluid distribution to the PoolManager, so this part is unconfirmed. Such a credit would be paid by the distributor and would give no gain, and the credited amount could not be taken while the block stands. collectProtocolFees cannot be called on Celo today because protocolFeeController() returns the zero address, so the statement about fee collection holds in code only. The actor value issuer is right: only an account with the admin role of the token can set or lift the block, and no step is open to an ordinary account.

With from set to the PoolManager, transfer(recipient, 0) returns true and transfers of 1 and of 10^18 revert with 0x206e5f37 followed by (false, amount, 0). I computed that selector locally from UnauthorizedPoolManagerTransfer(bool,uint256,uint256). authorizePoolManagerTransfer(bool,uint256) returns without error when the caller is the hook address and reverts with 0x67373552, which the signature database names NotCanonicalHook(), for the PoolManager and for an unrelated caller. poolManagerTransferBudget(bool) returns 0 for both flag values outside a transaction. The selectors of setPoolManagerGate(bool), setHook(address) and setBlockedVenue(address,bool) are present in the bytecode. GeckoTerminal lists an ELO / HYPE 1% pool with about 90,000 USD of reserves. v4CRCL on X Layer, https://rpc.xlayer.tech at block 76,626,622: name() is Uniswap v4 Circle - Securitize, POOL_MANAGER() is the PoolManager, PERMISSIONED_TOKEN() is 0x76163273f8bae6570ba3bb202044129a98e98f16 (symbol CRCL, 6 decimals), allowListChecker() is 0x09e4ef4da58d13edcc8c10d02c89dd8ed119f9ec and swappingEnabled() is 1. totalSupply() and balanceOf(PoolManager) are both 68,536,255 base units, and the wrapper holds the same amount of CRCL. verdicts.codeCheck: take books the debit and calls transfer on the currency with the PoolManager as msg.sender (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, src/types/Currency.sol:60-74). A revert in the token makes the take revert with the wrapped ERC20TransferFailed error (src/types/Currency.sol:82-86), and the same holds for collectProtocolFees (src/ProtocolFees.sol:56). burn credits the caller and makes no token call, so a claim can be burned at any time and only the take that follows depends on the token (src/PoolManager.sol:332-336). Each take is debited in full before the call and a zero amount take books nothing (src/PoolManager.sol:294, 368-369), so the token rules give an ordinary account no credit and no payout in another currency. I agree with the finding that no path leads from these two tokens to other pools.
verdicts.corrections: The sentence that a pool with another hook or with no hook can receive ELO and can never pay it out is wrong for the receiving half. A transfer of 1 base unit to the PoolManager from each of four ELO holders reverts with UnauthorizedPoolManagerTransfer(true, 1, 0), so ELO can neither enter nor leave the PoolManager without a budget from the hook. The statement that the owner can replace the hook did not hold in simulation: setHook from the owner address reverts with 0xbef9156a, which the signature database names HookAlreadySet(). setPoolManagerGate(false) from the owner succeeds in simulation and reverts for another caller, so the owner can open the gate. The v4CRCL balance is now 68.54 and the finding quotes 65.98. Not confirmed: verified source for either token, the logic of the ELO hook and who controls it, and a payout of v4CRCL to a permitted recipient, because I did not find an address on the permission list. The actor value pool-creator fits ELO. For v4CRCL the party that decides payouts is the keeper of the permission list of the underlying security token, which is closer to issuer. Neither is an ordinary account. Severity low stands: the payout dependence on the hook is the hazard the state already records for hooks, and the sums are about 46,000 USD and under 2,000 USD.

verdicts.factCheck: On https://api.avax.network/ext/bc/C/rpc at block 101,117,710 on 2026-11-23: qiAVAX at 0x5C0401e81Bc07Ca70fAD469b451682c0d747Ef1c names 0x486af39519b4dc9a7fccd318217352830e8ad9b4 as comptroller, and that contract names QI at 0x8729438eb15e2c8b576fcc6aecda6a148776c0f5. qiAVAX.balanceOf(PoolManager) is 230,561,327,030 (2,305.61 with 8 decimals). rewardAccrued(0, PoolManager) is 14.844 QI and rewardAccrued(1, PoolManager) is 0.1286 AVAX. QI.balanceOf(Comptroller) is 0.1096 QI and QI.balanceOf(PoolManager) is 10,974.54 QI. transfer(recipient, 0) with from set to the PoolManager returns true, and eth_estimateGas for it gives 167,537 for the whole transaction, which agrees with about 140,000 for the token call. claimReward(0, PoolManager) from an unrelated address returns without error. claimReward(1, PoolManager) reverts with the string Transfer failed. Through the Multicall3 contract that exists on chain I read QI.balanceOf(PoolManager), called claimReward(0, PoolManager) and read the balance again in one eth_call: the balance stayed at 10,974,542,456,766,585,212,156 and rewardAccrued stayed at 14.844 QI. The Comptroller source in the Benqi repository matches this behaviour: transferAllowed runs the supplier reward update for source and destination (lines 595 to 611), claimReward(uint8,address payable) is public (line 1234), and grantRewardInternal pays QI only when the amount is at most the balance of the Comptroller and otherwise leaves the accrual in place (lines 1287 to 1306). The AVAX branch sends value with 4,029 gas and requires success, which fails for a recipient without a receive function. The Routescan balance list shows 2,305.61 qiAVAX, 131.06 sAVAX and 10,974.54 QI for the PoolManager.
verdicts.codeCheck: take with amount 0 passes toInt128, and _accountDelta returns at once for a zero delta (src/PoolManager.sol:294, 368-369). The library still makes the CALL to the token with the PoolManager as msg.sender (src/types/Currency.sol:60-74), so any account inside an unlock can run the token's sender side logic at no cost. sync has no lock check and stores balanceOf(PoolManager) (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288). _settle credits the caller with the whole rise since the sync (src/PoolManager.sol:358-364), and take pays it out (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). The caller ends with all deltas at zero, so the count check in unlock passes (src/PoolManager.sol:112). No function in src/ pays out a balance surplus to pools: collectProtocolFees is limited to protocolFeesAccrued (src/ProtocolFees.sol:54-56). A QI payment that reaches the PoolManager between sync(QI) and settle is therefore credited to whoever opened the window. The guard at src/PoolManager.sol:356 does not apply because no value is sent. The path is the one already recorded for Ethereum under this reference.
verdicts.corrections: The zero amount transfer is not needed. claimReward updates the supply index and distributes to the holder by itself before it pays. The impact line about what accrues later needs a number: supplyRewardSpeeds(0, qiAVAX) and supplyRewardSpeeds(1, qiAVAX) both return 1 wei per second, and rewardAccrued rose by 103 wei across my claim simulation, so nothing of size accrues now. The 14.84 QI is a remainder from an earlier reward period. Today the claim pays nothing because the Comptroller holds 0.1096 QI, as the finding says. A caller who tops up the Comptroller himself to make the claim pay gains at most that 0.1096 QI. I compared the public repository file with on-chain behaviour only and did not match it to the deployed implementation bytecode. The actor value unprivileged is right, since the claim and every PoolManager call are open to any account. Severity low stands: the amount is small, the condition for a payout does not hold today, and pool principal is not touched.

clearedSpotChecks.check: L-166 on the OP Stack chains: all addresses with code among the 256 predeploy slots and the legacy ETH address, with the stub as an inner caller, and on Celo the CELO token at 0x471EcE3750Da237f93B8E339c536989b8978a438 as a second id over the native balance.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I repeated the Celo part, where a mistake would cost the most, with the on-chain Multicall3 code placed at the PoolManager address by state override in one eth_call on https://forno.celo.org at block 83,495,138. CELO.balanceOf(PoolManager) and the native balance both read 6,167,151,836,241,617,055,206. transfer(recipient, 1) lowered both by exactly 1. transfer(recipient, 0) and a transfer of 5 to the PoolManager itself left both unchanged. A transfer of 1 to the token address lowered both by 1 and a transfer to the zero address reverted. A value call of 10^12 wei from the PoolManager to the token reverts, and a value call of 1 wei to the PoolManager with empty calldata reverts. In code, a native credit needs settle with value while the synced currency slot is zero, and a settle with value reverts while a token is synced (src/PoolManager.sol:353-356). The slot is one transient word (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:15-32) and settle and settleFor are the only payable functions (src/PoolManager.sol:300-307), so one inflow is credited under one id. Deltas are stored per currency id (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:10-16), so a credit under one face cannot cancel a debt under the other. The wrapped native predeploy at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 raised balanceOf(PoolManager) by exactly 10^12 for a value call of 10^12 wei and paid out one to one on all ten OP Stack chains in my run. I did not repeat the sweep of the other 255 predeploy slots.

clearedSpotChecks.check: L-166 on Arc, where the face of the native asset uses another unit: the full cycle across address(0) (18 decimals) and 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000 (6 decimals), and whether native value can be forced into the PoolManager.
clearedSpotChecks.note: On https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io at block 32,653,454 (client arc/v1) the native balance of the PoolManager is 2,445,277,950,504,539,038,543,176 wei and the face reports 2,445,277,950,504, which is the floor of the native balance divided by 10^12. With a balance override of 5,999,999,999,999 wei the face reports 5 and with 6,000,000,000,000 it reports 6. With Multicall3 code placed at the PoolManager address, transfer(recipient, 1) on the face lowered the face balance by 1 and the native balance by exactly 10^12, and a zero amount transfer and a transfer to itself changed nothing. A value call from the PoolManager to the face is refused with the message Blocked address, and a value call of 1 wei to the PoolManager reverts. A credit under the face id is floor((B + x) / 10^12) minus floor(B / 10^12) for an inflow of x wei, which exceeds x / 10^12 by less than one unit, so the bound of 10^12 minus 1 wei per sync and settle pair is arithmetic. The gas price read 25 gwei, so 100,000 gas costs 2.5 * 10^15 wei. Even at a gas price of zero a 30,000,000 gas block holds a few hundred rounds, which is under 0.001 USDC per block. I did not repeat the creation probe that shows a self destruct can force wei into the PoolManager. The bound does not depend on it.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Lead L-166, method for all 21 networks: the EntryPoints and the wrapped native token raise balanceOf(PoolManager) by exactly the value sent, the EntryPoints reject transfer, no address raises its ledger on a zero value call or a zero amount transfer, and the full cycle leaves the caller with what a direct deposit gives.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I ran my own probe on all 21 endpoints of networks.json on 2026-11-23, with Multicall3 code at the PoolManager address by state override: balanceOf, a value call of 10^12 wei with empty calldata, a zero value call, transfer(recipient, 0) and transfer(recipient, 10^12), with balanceOf read after each. EntryPoint v0.6, v0.7 and v0.8 raised balanceOf(PoolManager) by exactly 10^12 on the value call, by 0 on the zero value call, and failed both transfers on 20 networks. The v0.8 probe on Monad was cut off by a rate limit. Tempo refuses the call with the message value transfer not allowed. The wrapped native token gave plus 10^12, 0, 0 and minus 10^12 on Ethereum, the ten OP Stack chains, Arbitrum One, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche and HyperEVM. I did not test the wrapped native token on Robinhood Chain, Elysium, Monad and Arc. On Avalanche sAVAX minted 771,420,171,255 units for 10^12 wei and rejects a zero amount transfer, and qiAVAX minted 4,276 units. The accounting argument holds in code: the native take is debited in full before the CALL (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295), settle credits only the measured rise under the synced id (src/PoolManager.sol:358-364), and unlock needs every delta at zero (src/PoolManager.sol:112), so the caller pays the native debt with value of its own. I did not repeat the sweep of 248 pooled tokens. For five of them on Celo (WBRL, WARS, USDC, USDT, USDm) a zero amount transfer, a transfer of 1 and a transfer to itself from the PoolManager changed the balance by exactly 0, minus 1 and 0.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Can take make the PoolManager call itself with effect, so that its own ERC-6909 ledger serves as a mirrored ledger?
clearedSpotChecks.note: Code reading only. The ERC-20 call uses selector a9059cbb with two arguments (src/types/Currency.sol:60-62) and sync uses balanceOf(address) (src/types/Currency.sol:94). The PoolManager's own transfer and balanceOf take three and two arguments (src/ERC6909.sol:17, 25), so their selectors differ. A search of src/ outside src/test and of lib/solmate/src/auth/Owned.sol finds no fallback and no receive function, and settle and settleFor are the only payable functions (src/PoolManager.sol:300-307). A take, a sync or a native payout that names the PoolManager reverts.

leads.question: Can a Superfluid distribution to the PoolManager, or a public claim made on its behalf for a distribution pool, raise G$.balanceOf(PoolManager) while the address is blocked, and is any such amount pending for it today?
leads.why: The verified SuperGoodDollar source says a blocked account can still be credited by agreements, and the finding states that no increase can occur. A claim that any account can make for the PoolManager would be one more balance rise that sync and settle book to the caller (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364). The credited G$ could not be taken while the block stands, so the expected result is a clearance with a corrected statement.
